claim: Orexin neurons are exclusively located in the lateral hypothalamus (LH) and adjacent regions in the brain, including the perifornical area, and dorsomedial and posterior hypothalamus.
source: Orexin neurons are exclusively located in the lateral hypothalamus (LH) and adjacent regions in the brain, including the perifornical area, and dorsomedial and posterior hypothalamus (Soya and Sakurai, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Soya and Sakurai, 2020

claim: Abundant orexin fibers innervate the ventral tegmental area (VTA) and substantia nigra (SN).
source: Abundant orexin fibers innervate the ventral tegmental area (VTA) and substantia nigra (SN), which together contain the majority of dopaminergic neurons in humans and rodents (Fadel and Deutch, 2002; Hrabovszky et al., 2013; Peyron et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fadel and Deutch, 2002; Hrabovszky et al., 2013; Peyron et al., 1998

claim: The VTA and SN together contain the majority of dopaminergic neurons in humans and rodents.
source: Abundant orexin fibers innervate the ventral tegmental area (VTA) and substantia nigra (SN), which together contain the majority of dopaminergic neurons in humans and rodents (Fadel and Deutch, 2002; Hrabovszky et al., 2013; Peyron et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fadel and Deutch, 2002; Hrabovszky et al., 2013; Peyron et al., 1998

claim: There are some dopaminergic neurons in other brain regions, although not all of these neurons express the dopamine transporter (DAT).
source: There are also some dopaminergic neurons in other brain regions, although not all of these neurons express the dopamine transporter (DAT) (Koblinger et al., 2018; Sharples et al., 2014; Turiault et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Koblinger et al., 2018; Sharples et al., 2014; Turiault et al., 2007

claim: Both the orexin and dopaminergic systems control food intake, locomotor activity, reward processing as well as energy metabolism.
source: Both the orexin and dopaminergic systems control food intake, locomotor activity, reward processing as well as energy metabolism (Howe and Dombeck, 2016; Inutsuka and Yamanaka, 2013; Narayanan et al., 2010; Palmiter, 2007; Tsujino and Sakurai, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Howe and Dombeck, 2016; Inutsuka and Yamanaka, 2013; Narayanan et al., 2010; Palmiter, 2007; Tsujino and Sakurai, 2013

claim: Dopamine was discovered as a neuro-active molecule approximately 70 years ago.
source: Dopamine was discovered as a neuro-active molecule approximately 70 y ago and the dopaminergic system has diverse functions (Iversen and Iversen, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Iversen and Iversen, 2007

claim: The dopaminergic system has diverse functions.
source: Dopamine was discovered as a neuro-active molecule approximately 70 y ago and the dopaminergic system has diverse functions (Iversen and Iversen, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Iversen and Iversen, 2007

claim: The nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, containing the dopaminergic projections from SN to the dorsal striatum, predominantly regulates action selection and exploratory behaviors.
source: In a simplified model the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, containing the dopaminergic projections from SN to the dorsal striatum, predominantly regulates action selection and exploratory behaviors.
evidence: Stated as part of a simplified model in the manuscript text

claim: The mesolimbic and mesocortical dopaminergic systems, which consist of the dopaminergic pathways from the VTA to the ventral striatum and prefrontal cortex, predominantly regulate motivation, cognition, decision-making, reward, and aversive behavior.
source: In contrast, the mesolimbic and mesocortical dopaminergic systems, which consist of the dopaminergic pathways from the VTA to the ventral striatum and prefrontal cortex, predominantly regulate motivation, cognition, decision-making, reward, and aversive behavior (Kutlu et al., 2021; Latif et al., 2021; Lerner et al., 2021; Roeper, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kutlu et al., 2021; Latif et al., 2021; Lerner et al., 2021; Roeper, 2013

claim: Some VTA dopaminergic neurons represent movements in trained animals.
source: Some VTA dopaminergic neurons also represent movements in trained animals (Lerner et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lerner et al., 2021

claim: Dopaminergic neurons modulate movement differently via direct and indirect pathways through the striatum.
source: Dopaminergic neurons modulate movement differently via direct and indirect pathways through the striatum (Kim et al., 2017; Kreitzer and Malenka, 2008; Roseberry et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kim et al., 2017; Kreitzer and Malenka, 2008; Roseberry et al., 2016

claim: Co-release of other neuro-active molecules by dopaminergic terminals could affect the precision and diversity of dopaminergic functions.
source: Co-release of other neuro-active molecules by dopaminergic terminals (Barcomb and Ford, 2023; Buck et al., 2021; Zych and Ford, 2022) and the spatial and temporal dynamics of dopamine release (Berke, 2018; Chantranupong et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2021) could further affect the precision and diversity of dopaminergic functions.
evidence: Supported by citations to Barcomb and Ford, 2023; Buck et al., 2021; Zych and Ford, 2022

claim: The spatial and temporal dynamics of dopamine release could affect the precision and diversity of dopaminergic functions.
source: Co-release of other neuro-active molecules by dopaminergic terminals (Barcomb and Ford, 2023; Buck et al., 2021; Zych and Ford, 2022) and the spatial and temporal dynamics of dopamine release (Berke, 2018; Chantranupong et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2021) could further affect the precision and diversity of dopaminergic functions.
evidence: Supported by citations to Berke, 2018; Chantranupong et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2021

claim: Orexin A injection into the VTA increases cocaine- and morphine-related reward processing.
source: Orexin A injection into the VTA increases cocaine- and morphine-related reward processing (Mahler et al., 2012), and intra-SN injection of orexin A induces hyperlocomotion and stereotypic behaviors (Liu et al., 2018; Nakamura et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mahler et al., 2012

claim: Intra-SN injection of orexin A induces hyperlocomotion and stereotypic behaviors.
source: Orexin A injection into the VTA increases cocaine- and morphine-related reward processing (Mahler et al., 2012), and intra-SN injection of orexin A induces hyperlocomotion and stereotypic behaviors (Liu et al., 2018; Nakamura et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2018; Nakamura et al., 2000

claim: Systemic injection of dopamine receptor antagonists reduces orexin A-induced increase of hyperlocomotion, and stereotypic and grooming behaviors.
source: On the other hand, systemic injection of dopamine receptor antagonists reduces orexin A-induced increase of hyperlocomotion, and stereotypic and grooming behaviors (Nakamura et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nakamura et al., 2000

claim: Whether the effects of orexin signaling in the VTA and SN are mediated by dopaminergic or non-dopaminergic cells is not yet clear.
source: However, whether the above effects of orexin signaling in the VTA and SN are mediated by dopaminergic or non-dopaminergic cells is not yet clear.
evidence: Stated as an open question in the manuscript

claim: The orexin system consists of the two peptides orexin A and B, which are derived from the precursor, prepro-orexin.
source: The orexin system consists of the two peptides orexin A and B, which are derived from the precursor, prepro-orexin (de Lecea et al., 1998; Sakurai et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to de Lecea et al., 1998; Sakurai et al., 1998

claim: Orexin A and B are endogenous ligands for two G-protein-coupled receptors, orexin receptor subtype 1 (Ox1R), and 2 (Ox2R).
source: Both are endogenous ligands for two G-protein-coupled receptors, orexin receptor subtype 1 (Ox1R), and 2 (Ox2R) (Sakurai et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sakurai et al., 1998

claim: Orexin A activates both Ox1R and Ox2R receptors.
source: Orexin A activates both receptors, while orexin B predominantly activates Ox2R (Sakurai et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sakurai et al., 1998

claim: Orexin B predominantly activates Ox2R.
source: Orexin A activates both receptors, while orexin B predominantly activates Ox2R (Sakurai et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sakurai et al., 1998

claim: Detection of mRNA by in situ hybridization revealed the expression of both Ox1R and Ox2R receptors in the VTA and SN.
source: Detection of mRNA by in situ hybridization revealed the expression of both receptors in the VTA and SN (Marcus et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Marcus et al., 2001

claim: The cell-type specific expression of Ox1R and Ox2R in the VTA and SN is not well understood.
source: However, the cell-type specific expression of Ox1R and Ox2R in the VTA and SN is not well understood.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap in the manuscript

claim: Electrophysiological studies showed that orexin receptors are present in dopaminergic VTA neurons.
source: Electrophysiological studies showed that orexin receptors are present in dopaminergic VTA neurons (Baimel et al., 2017; Korotkova et al., 2003; Tung et al., 2016), whereas data for the SN seem controversial (Korotkova et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Baimel et al., 2017; Korotkova et al., 2003; Tung et al., 2016

claim: Data for orexin receptor presence in dopaminergic SN neurons seem controversial.
source: Electrophysiological studies showed that orexin receptors are present in dopaminergic VTA neurons (Baimel et al., 2017; Korotkova et al., 2003; Tung et al., 2016), whereas data for the SN seem controversial (Korotkova et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Korotkova et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2018

claim: In control mice, Ox1R was expressed in 44–58% of dopaminergic neurons in all VTA and SN sub-regions.
source: In control mice, Ox1R was expressed in 44–58% of dopaminergic neurons in all VTA and SN sub-regions, including the interfascicular (IF), paranigral (PN), parainterfascicular (PIF), and parabrachial (PBP) subnuclei of the VTA and SN.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNAscope in situ hybridization shown in Figure 1

claim: Ox2R-positive dopaminergic neurons were mainly located in the medial VTA, including IF, PN, and PIF, with 25–42% of dopaminergic neurons expressing the Ox2R.
source: In contrast, Ox2R-positive dopaminergic neurons were mainly located in the medial VTA, including IF, PN, and PIF, with 25–42% of dopaminergic neurons expressing the Ox2R (Figure 1A, C, D, G-I; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNAscope in situ hybridization shown in Figure 1A, C, D, G-I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: 47–59% of dopaminergic neurons expressed Ox1R in all VTA and SN sub-regions.
source: Thus, we could analyze the distribution of Ox1R-, Ox2R-, Ox1R, and Ox2R-, and none (of orexin receptors)-expressing dopaminergic neurons in each VTA subregion and the SN (Figure 1J). The results were similar to the above: 47–59% of dopaminergic neurons expressed Ox1R in all VTA and SN sub-regions, and Ox2R was mainly expressed by 26–41% of dopaminergic neurons in the medial VTA (Figure 1J).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J

claim: Ox2R was mainly expressed by 26–41% of dopaminergic neurons in the medial VTA.
source: Thus, we could analyze the distribution of Ox1R-, Ox2R-, Ox1R, and Ox2R-, and none (of orexin receptors)-expressing dopaminergic neurons in each VTA subregion and the SN (Figure 1J). The results were similar to the above: 47–59% of dopaminergic neurons expressed Ox1R in all VTA and SN sub-regions, and Ox2R was mainly expressed by 26–41% of dopaminergic neurons in the medial VTA (Figure 1J).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J

claim: 19–25% of dopaminergic neurons in the medial VTA expressed both Ox1R and Ox2R.
source: 19–25% of dopaminergic neurons in the medial VTA expressed both Ox1R and Ox2R (Figure 1J).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J

claim: Abundant Ox1R and Ox2R expression was present in Th-negative neurons in the VTA, SN, and neighboring regions.
source: Of note, abundant Ox1R and Ox2R expression was present in Th-negative neurons in the VTA, SN, and neighboring regions (Figure 1A, C, D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: In Ox1RΔDAT mice, Ox1R expression was significantly reduced in dopaminergic neurons and remained unchanged in Th-negative cells.
source: In Ox1RΔDAT mice, Ox1R expression was significantly reduced in dopaminergic neurons and remained unchanged in Th-negative cells (Figure 1B, E-I; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, E-I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: The Ox2R expression patterns remained similar to that in the control mice in Ox1RΔDAT mice, indicating the successful and specific knockout of Ox1R in dopaminergic neurons.
source: In contrast, the Ox2R expression patterns remained similar to that in the control mice, indicating the successful and specific knockout of Ox1R in dopaminergic neurons (Figure 1B, E, I; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, E, I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: Orexin A activates dopaminergic neurons in the mouse SN.
source: Next, we used perforated patch clamp recordings to establish that orexin A activates dopaminergic neurons not only in the mouse VTA (e.g. Baimel et al., 2017; Korotkova et al., 2003; Tung et al., 2016), but also in the mouse SN (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from perforated patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: In dopaminergic SN neurons that were pharmacologically isolated from GABAergic and glutamatergic synaptic input, 100 nM orexin increased the action potential frequency in 75% (6 of 8) of the neurons.
source: In dopaminergic SN neurons that were pharmacologically isolated from GABAerigc and glutamatergic synaptic input 100 nM orexin increased the action potential frequency in 75% (6 of 8) of the neurons.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from perforated patch clamp recordings

claim: Increasing the orexin A concentration to 300 nM further increased the firing frequency in dopaminergic SN neurons.
source: Increasing the orexin A concentration to 300 nM further increased the firing frequency.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from perforated patch clamp recordings

claim: The finding that orexin A increases firing frequency in dopaminergic SN neurons is consistent with previous extracellular recordings in rats.
source: This finding is consistent with previous extracellular recordings in rats (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2018

claim: Bath application of 100 nM orexin A resulted in a clear and significant increase in [Ca2+]i in dopaminergic SN control neurons.
source: Bath application of 100 nM orexin A already resulted in a clear and significant increase in [Ca2+]i in dopaminergic SN control neurons (Figure 1I-L, Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Ca2+ imaging shown in Figure 1I-L and Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4

claim: 56% of dopaminergic SN control neurons tested responded to 100 nM orexin A, while 44% of the neurons did not respond.
source: We found that 56% of the neurons tested responded to 100 nM orexin A, while 44% of the neurons did not respond (Figure 1L, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Ca2+ imaging shown in Figure 1L and Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: The percentage of dopaminergic SN neurons responding to orexin A (56%) is in very good agreement with the number of Ox1R-expressing neurons.
source: These data are in very good agreement with the number of Ox1R-expressing neurons (Figure 1J).
evidence: Inference based on comparison of Ca2+ imaging data with RNAscope data shown in Figure 1J

claim: Control neurons showed a highly significant and marked response to 100 nM orexin A (p<0.0001, n=71), while the Ox1R knockout neurons did not respond (p=0.5, n=86).
source: We found a highly significant and marked response of control neurons to 100 nM orexin A, while the Ox1R knockout neurons did not respond (control: p<0.0001, n=71; Ox1RΔDAT: p=0.5, n=86; one sample t-test for each group) (Figure 1L).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Ca2+ imaging shown in Figure 1L with statistical analysis

claim: Ox1R is the main orexin receptor expressed in dopaminergic VTA and SN neurons and mediates their activation by orexin.
source: In conclusion, Ox1R is the main orexin receptor expressed in dopaminergic VTA and SN neurons and mediates their activation by orexin.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from RNAscope and Ca2+ imaging data

claim: Ox1RΔDAT mice did not show significant changes in spontaneous locomotor activity in home cages compared to controls.
source: Compared to controls, Ox1RΔDAT mice did not show significant changes in spontaneous locomotor activity in home cages (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: When exposed to a novel open field, male and female Ox1RΔDAT mice exhibited an increase in locomotion and exploration, with increased traveling distance, ambulating time, and vertical activity.
source: When exposed to a novel open field, male and female Ox1RΔDAT mice exhibited an increase in locomotion and exploration, with increased traveling distance, ambulating time, and vertical activity in the open field test (Figure 2A–C and E–G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A–C and E–G

claim: Female Ox1RΔDAT mice showed increased stereotypic activity in the open field test.
source: Female Ox1RΔDAT mice also showed increased stereotypic activity (Figure 2D and H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and H

claim: Intracerebroventricular (ICV) injection of orexin A (1 nmol) induced a more pronounced increase of locomotor activity in both female and male Ox1RΔDAT mice, compared to control mice.
source: Furthermore, intracerebroventricular (ICV) injection of orexin A (1 nmol) induced a more pronounced increase of locomotor activity in both female and male Ox1RΔDAT mice, compared to control mice (Figure 2I–L).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I–L

claim: Female Ox1RΔDAT mice showed increased nose pokes into the holes in early (1st and 2nd) sessions compared to control mice in a hole-board test.
source: In a hole-board test, female Ox1RΔDAT mice showed increased nose pokes into the holes in early (1st and 2nd) sessions compared to control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B

claim: The increased nose pokes in female Ox1RΔDAT mice disappeared later when mice became familiar with the environment (third – eighth session).
source: This effect disappeared later when mice became familiar with the environment (third – eighth session) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B

claim: In the novel object recognition test, female Ox1RΔDAT mice spent more time with each of the two identical objects in an open field compared to control mice.
source: In the novel object recognition test, female Ox1RΔDAT mice spent more time with each of the two identical objects in an open field compared to control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E

claim: One hour later, when female mice were exposed to the same environment except that one object was replaced by a novel object, there was no significant difference between control and Ox1RΔDAT mice in exploring the novel object.
source: One hour later, when female mice were exposed to the same environment except that one object was replaced by a novel object, there was no significant difference between control and Ox1RΔDAT mice in exploring the novel object (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F

claim: Male Ox1RΔDAT mice did not behave differently in the hole-board and novel object recognition tests from controls.
source: In contrast, male Ox1RΔDAT mice did not behave differently in the hole-board and novel object recognition tests from controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, C, D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, C, D

claim: Ox1R signaling in dopaminergic neurons is more important for females in novelty-induced exploration, which was independent of novel object discrimination.
source: This indicates that Ox1R signaling in dopaminergic neurons is more important for females in novelty-induced exploration, which was independent of novel object discrimination.
evidence: Inference based on behavioral data showing sex differences

claim: The behavioral changes seemed not related to alterations in anxiety since there were no detectable changes in anxiety-related behaviors.
source: The behavioral changes seemed not related to alterations in anxiety since there were no detectable changes in anxiety-related behaviors, including the time spent in and the times of entries into the center area, light side, and the open arms in an open field test, dark/light box test and 0-maze test, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3

claim: In both of the control and Ox1RΔDAT groups, the percentages of the consumption of 1% sucrose, 2% sucrose, and 0.04% sucralose solution in the total drinking were higher than 50%, indicating the preference for sweet solution.
source: In both of the control and Ox1RΔDAT groups, the percentages of the consumption of 1% sucrose, 2% sucrose, and 0.04% sucralose solution in the total drinking were higher than 50%, indicating the preference for sweet solution, though only female control mice showed a significant preference of 0.5% sucrose solution, analyzed by a one-sample t-test (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, D

claim: There was no significant difference between control and Ox1RΔDAT groups in sweet solution preference by two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak's post hoc test.
source: There was no significant difference between the two groups by two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak's post hoc test (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, B, D, E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, B, D, E

claim: All groups except the male control group showed a significant preference for cocaine injection using a one-sample t-test in the CPP test.
source: All groups except the male control group showed a significant preference for cocaine injection using a one-sample t-test, and there was no significant difference between control and Ox1RΔDAT groups by unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, F

claim: There was no significant difference between control and Ox1RΔDAT groups in cocaine CPP by unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test.
source: All groups except the male control group showed a significant preference for cocaine injection using a one-sample t-test, and there was no significant difference between control and Ox1RΔDAT groups by unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, F

claim: Neither male nor female Ox1RΔDAT mice showed significant changes in energy metabolism, including body weight, fat mass, respiratory exchanging ratio, energy expenditure, daily food intake, glucose tolerance, and insulin sensitivity.
source: In addition, neither male nor female Ox1RΔDAT mice showed significant changes in energy metabolism, including body weight, fat mass, respiratory exchanging ratio, energy expenditure, daily food intake, glucose tolerance, and insulin sensitivity (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5

claim: In Ox1RΔDAT mice under control conditions (saline injection), higher neuronal activity was observed around the medial preoptic area (MPA), piriform cortex (Pir), endopiriform claustrum, lateral stripe of the striatum (LSS), ventral part of subcoeruleus nucleus (SubCV), spinal trigeminal nucleus, spinal trigeminal tract (sp5), the intermediate reticular zone (IRt) and the gigantocellular reticular nucleus (Gi) than control mice.
source: In Ox1RΔDAT mice under control conditions (saline injection), we observed higher neuronal activity around the medial preoptic area (MPA), piriform cortex (Pir), endopiriform claustrum, lateral stripe of the striatum (LSS), ventral part of subcoeruleus nucleus (SubCV), spinal trigeminal nucleus, spinal trigeminal tract (sp5), the intermediate reticular zone (IRt) and the gigantocellular reticular nucleus (Gi) than control mice (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 1A and 2).
evidence: Supported by PET imaging data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplements 1A and 2

claim: Compared to control mice, central application of orexin A (1 nmol, ICV) to Ox1RΔDAT mice induced higher neuronal activity around the LPGi, the nucleus of the horizontal limb of the diagonal band (HDB) and magnocellular preoptic nucleus (MCPO).
source: Compared to control mice, central application of orexin A (1 nmol, ICV) to Ox1RΔDAT mice induced higher neuronal activity around the LPGi, the nucleus of the horizontal limb of the diagonal band (HDB) and magnocellular preoptic nucleus (MCPO), and lower activity around secondary motor cortex (M2), the dorsal bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), the hindlimb, shoulder, and trunk regions and barrel field of primary somatosensory cortex (S1HL, S1Sh, S1Tr, and S1BF), the lateral area of secondary visual cortex (V2L), primary visual cortex (V1), Pir and dorsal endopiriform claustrum (DEn) (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplements 1B and 2).
evidence: Supported by PET imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplements 1B and 2

claim: Compared to control mice, central application of orexin A (1 nmol, ICV) to Ox1RΔDAT mice induced lower neuronal activity around secondary motor cortex (M2), the dorsal bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), the hindlimb, shoulder, and trunk regions and barrel field of primary somatosensory cortex (S1HL, S1Sh, S1Tr, and S1BF), the lateral area of secondary visual cortex (V2L), primary visual cortex (V1), Pir and dorsal endopiriform claustrum (DEn).
source: Compared to control mice, central application of orexin A (1 nmol, ICV) to Ox1RΔDAT mice induced higher neuronal activity around the LPGi, the nucleus of the horizontal limb of the diagonal band (HDB) and magnocellular preoptic nucleus (MCPO), and lower activity around secondary motor cortex (M2), the dorsal bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), the hindlimb, shoulder, and trunk regions and barrel field of primary somatosensory cortex (S1HL, S1Sh, S1Tr, and S1BF), the lateral area of secondary visual cortex (V2L), primary visual cortex (V1), Pir and dorsal endopiriform claustrum (DEn) (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplements 1B and 2).
evidence: Supported by PET imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplements 1B and 2

claim: PET imaging did not reveal significant changes in the VTA and SN.
source: PET imaging did not reveal significant changes in the VTA and SN (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by PET imaging data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Postmortem analysis of c-Fos staining revealed low c-Fos expression in dopaminergic neurons in the VTA and SN of Ox1RΔDAT and control mice after ICV injection of saline or orexin A (1 nmol).
source: Postmortem analysis of c-Fos staining revealed low c-Fos expression in dopaminergic neurons in the VTA and SN of Ox1RΔDAT and control mice after ICV injection of saline or orexin A (1 nmol).
evidence: Supported by c-Fos staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: No apparent changes in c-Fos expression in dopaminergic neurons were observed among the groups after ICV injection of saline or orexin A.
source: No apparent changes were observed among the groups.
evidence: Supported by c-Fos staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: Clear orexin-induced c-Fos activity was observed in non-dopaminergic cells in the VTA and SN.
source: In contrast, clear orexin-induced c-Fos activity was observed in non-dopaminergic cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by c-Fos staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: The dorsal BNST and LPGi play a key functional role in regulating emotion, exploratory behaviors, and locomotor speed, which are related to novelty-induced locomotion.
source: They play a key functional role in regulating emotion, exploratory behaviors, and locomotor speed, which are related to novelty-induced locomotion (Arber and Costa, 2022; Avery et al., 2016; Capelli et al., 2017; Crestani et al., 2013; Giardino et al., 2018; Takatoh et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Arber and Costa, 2022; Avery et al., 2016; Capelli et al., 2017; Crestani et al., 2013; Giardino et al., 2018; Takatoh et al., 2013

claim: Dopaminergic projections were discovered in the dorsal BNST and LPGi after injecting Cre-dependent AAV-EYFP bilaterally into the VTA and SN of DAT-Cre mice.
source: To this end, we injected Cre-dependent AAV-EYFP bilaterally into the VTA and SN of DAT-Cre (DATEYFP) and Ox1RΔDAT (DATΔOx1R; EYFP) mice, and discovered dopaminergic projections in the dorsal BNST and LPGi (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), suggesting that VTA and SN dopaminergic neurons could directly modulate neuronal activity in the dorsal BNST and LPGi.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: VTA and SN dopaminergic neurons could directly modulate neuronal activity in the dorsal BNST and LPGi.
source: To this end, we injected Cre-dependent AAV-EYFP bilaterally into the VTA and SN of DAT-Cre (DATEYFP) and Ox1RΔDAT (DATΔOx1R; EYFP) mice, and discovered dopaminergic projections in the dorsal BNST and LPGi (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), suggesting that VTA and SN dopaminergic neurons could directly modulate neuronal activity in the dorsal BNST and LPGi.
evidence: Inference based on anatomical tracing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: Orexin A injection (1 nmol, ICV) induced higher c-Fos expression levels in LPGi of male Ox1RΔDAT mice compared to control mice.
source: Orexin A injection (1 nmol, ICV) induced higher c-Fos expression levels in LPGi of male Ox1RΔDAT mice compared to control mice (Figure 4A and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and C

claim: Only the inhibitory D2 but not excitatory D1 subtypes of dopamine receptors (DRD2, DRD1) could be detected in LPGi.
source: Only the inhibitory D2 but not excitatory D1 subtypes of dopamine receptors (DRD2, DRD1) could be detected in LPGi (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E

claim: Both DRD1 and DRD2 receptors were detected around the lateral ventricle (as positive control).
source: Both receptors were detected around the lateral ventricle (as positive control), whereas no signal was detectable in LPGi incubated with a negative control probe for mice (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F and G

claim: No signal was detectable in LPGi incubated with a negative control probe for mice.
source: Both receptors were detected around the lateral ventricle (as positive control), whereas no signal was detectable in LPGi incubated with a negative control probe for mice (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F and G
